direction: Out-of-run evaluation of the existing November 25 ranking. Keep fixed menu order, exact BM25, keyboard title cues, and ordinary smoke plus two candidate scenarios. No policy tuning or per-library action descriptions in this study.
population: Use the saved public closed-issue extension from November 18 for Flatpickr, Air Datepicker, Vanilla JS Datepicker and Bootstrap Datepicker, in its original round-robin order. Only ordinary UI and accessibility behavior. Exclude previously evaluated or prepared fixtures, duplicate behavior from the same upstream fix, support, enhancements, platform-only issues, and cases without an evidenced affected/fixed published pair.
strata: Flatpickr keyboard-triggered title with a changed schedule. Take first qualified remaining issue in November 25's same-order title queue.

Flatpickr no schedule change: closed issue title about range, dates or time with a reproducible public fix. Start with ordinary-function release-note references in the frozen archive, most recent releases and their listed order. Require a distinct behavior and repair from the first stratum.

Other library: take newest saved issue within each repo about date/time/range/navigation or a keyboard action, interleaved by original order. Require clear steps and affected plus fixed package evidence. Take at most two qualifying tickets, prefer distinct behaviors and repair PRs.
version_rule: Affected release named by reporter or defensible release current when reported, fixed release documented by maintainer/reproduction or earliest stable package after explicit merged fix. No version search by browser outcome.
acceptance: Before opening either build, save the actual published title, packages with digests, configuration, plans, and observable incident/control checks. Use original release bytes and finite local scenarios in Chrome. Full reference and candidate menus, fresh context per action. Reference passes every check. Candidate matches a publicly described failure and passes unrelated controls. Repeat target failure in new context. Keep all failures, technical errors, and null observations. One common control or erroneous setup correction is allowed per issue; preserve initial inputs and runs. Each qualified issue should be run again independently. Browser rounds and alternate fixtures never enlarge the issue denominator.
analysis: Log first hit, hit by step 2/3, exact order, displaced action, candidate and reference costs separately, and failure of promoted actions to help when visible. Pair within each case. All strategies use zero reference screenshots in search; retain verification screenshots. Leave the public repo untouched.
